title: Associate Director- Sustainability & Impact (Lyon, France)
description:
Location : Lyon, France 

About ARCHIMED: 

With offices in Europe, North America and Asia, ARCHIMED is a leading investment firm focused exclusively on healthcare industries. Its mix of operational, medical, scientific and financial expertise allows ARCHIMED to serve as both a strategic and financial partner to healthcare businesses. Prioritized areas of focus include Biopharma Products, Consumer Health, Healthcare IT, In Vitro Diagnostics, Life Science Tools & Biologic Services, MedTech, and Pharma Services. 

ARCHIMED helps partners internationalize, acquire, innovate and expand their products and services. ARCHIMED manages €8 billion across its various funds, including the largest healthcare-only private equity fund raised by a European-based General Partner. Since inception, ARCHIMED has been a committed Impact investor, both directly and through its EURÊKA Foundation.

The Team 

• An international team (with more than 30 nationalities) with complementary education and experience in the investment, medical, scientific, strategic and operational sectors

• Composed of alumni from: INSEAD, Berkeley, Georgetown, Bocconi, HEC Paris, Ponts et Chaussées, ESSEC, Imperial College, Dartmouth, etc.

• Professional backgrounds: Private Equity (3i, Siparex, USS Ltd, Barings, capiton), Consulting (A.T. Kearney, Bain, McKinsey), M&A (Lazard, EY, KPMG, PwC), Industry (Biotronik, Cerba, Pharmacy, Veterinary)

Your Role 

Portfolio engagement and value creation 

- Lead portfolio engagement on Sustainability and Impact (S&I), providing hands-on support to portfolio companies and tracking S&I progress across ARCHIMED’s portfolios through dashboards, KPIs, and supporting processes.
- Lead select portfolio value creation projects, collaborating with deal teams as well as guiding and project managing S&I interns where required.
- Develop and oversee the execution of actionable S&I roadmaps for each portfolio company, with targets and milestones based on the company’s materiality analysis and aligned with ARCHIMED’s S&I strategy, partnering with third-party technical experts when necessary.
- Influence portfolio company management to advance their roadmaps through technical guidance and sharing of best practices.
Investment process 

- Act as the bridge between deal teams and external providers during due diligence, critically assessing findings to confirm that each target is consistent with ARCHIMED’s S&I strategy and fund obligations.
- Work with all ARCHIMED functions to review and improve how S&I is integrated into investment decision making.
Data, reporting, and compliance 

- Establish the tools and framework to collect, monitor, and coordinate S&I data across funds, enabling timely, accurate, and consistent reporting, and select third-party technical experts when necessary.
- Analyze and interpret S&I data and substantially contribute to the production of ARCHIMED’s annual S&I report in line with industry standards and frameworks, turning data into clear narratives.
- Contribute substantially to regular reporting to investors and to mandatory disclosures on fund S&I performance, ensuring credibility and transparency.
- Monitor regulatory developments in ARCHIMED’s locations and sectors of focus, and help ensure compliance with sustainability-related requirements.
Center of excellence and capability building 

- Establish an S&I center of excellence across funds and portfolio companies, with tools, reports, and training materials that share guidance and best practices.
- Provide expert guidance and S&I training to management, investment, and investor relations teams to deepen integration across the business.
Requirements 

- At least 10 years’ experience building and executing sustainability strategies, preferably in private equity.
- Proven hands-on leadership, initiative, and project management skills, with strong problem-solving ability.
- Robust knowledge of S&I frameworks and disclosures, including SFDR, SASB, CSRD, EDCI, PMDR, and the UN SDGs.
- Strong command of impact measurement methodologies, including developing and reporting on impact metrics.
- Strong attention to detail, with the ability to build coherent sustainability narratives and proofread content.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills, with the adaptability to engage C-suite executives internationally.
- Proven team player, able to build working partnerships and promote collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders.
- Ability to coach junior team members, sharing knowledge and giving regular feedback.
- Pragmatic, constructive, creative, and solution-oriented, with a positive mindset and the ability to work under varied pressures.

- Strong command of impact measurement methodologies, including developing and reporting on impact metrics.
- Strong attention to detail, with the ability to build coherent sustainability narratives and proofread content.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills, with the adaptability to engage C-suite executives internationally.
- Proven team player, able to build working partnerships and promote collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders.
- Ability to coach junior team members, sharing knowledge and giving regular feedback.
- Pragmatic, constructive, creative, and solution-oriented, with a positive mindset and the ability to work under varied pressures.

title: Head of Performance Marketing – Meta Ads (m/w/d)
description:
❗️ Lies das, bevor du weiterscrollst: Das hier ist nichts für Einsteiger und nichts für Leute, die einen entspannten Job suchen. Wir suchen eine Marketing-Maschine : jemanden, der liefert, skaliert und uns zeigt, wie es geht, nicht andersherum.

Wenn du das bist, bekommst du bei uns Verantwortung, Freiraum und eine erfolgsabhängige Vergütung ohne Limit 🔥💸 Ob fest angestellt oder als Freelancer: Wichtig ist, dass du liefern kannst.

Wir sind ein junges, 2016 gegründetes E-Commerce Startup aus Minden. Wir vertreiben physische und digitale Produkte im Kosmetik-Nageldesign Bereich. 💅 Mit dem Lynis Nailshop und der Lynis-Nailacademy wollen wir schnell weiter wachsen. Im Marketing steckt das größte Potenzial, und genau dort fehlt uns die Person, die es hebt.

Du baust unser Performance Marketing auf Meta und das Team dahinter eigenständig auf. Wir geben dir Ziele, Budget und Vertrauen. Den Fahrplan bringst du mit. Am Anfang arbeitest du mit unserem bestehenden Team. In 12 Monaten steht unter deiner Führung ein eigenes Marketing-Team mit 3–5 Leuten. Dein Baby ist alles, was Marketing betrifft: Media Buying auf Meta, Funnels, Offers, Creatives, Zahlen und Menschen. Du entscheidest, wir erwarten Ergebnisse.

Aufgaben

- Meta aufbauen und skalieren: Du erkennst Chancen auf Meta, testest Zielgruppen, Kampagnen und Creatives und skalierst, was funktioniert. Und stoppst sofort, was nicht funktioniert.

- Funnels & Advertorials: Du baust performanceorientierte Funnels inklusive Advertorials und Landingpages und holst entlang des gesamten Funnels alles raus (Full-Funnel-Optimierung, CRO, A/B-Tests).

- Offer-Creation: Du entwickelst Offers, die sich verkaufen: für neue Zielgruppen und für Bestandskunden.

- Creatives & Copywriting: Du steuerst Ad-Scripting, Creative-Entwicklung und Copywriting und weißt, was konvertiert.

- KPIs & Controlling: Du lebst in den KPIs. Du analysierst alle Produkte und Kampagnen, optimierst laufend und steuerst Agenturen so, dass sie liefern.

- Team aufbauen und führen: Du stellst in den nächsten 12 Monaten ein eigenes Marketing-Team mit 3–5 Leuten zusammen, gibst Ziele vor, forderst Leistung ein und entwickelst deine Leute weiter. Bis dahin greifst du auf unser bestehendes Team zurück. Du entscheidest, wen du brauchst.

Klingt nach deinem Ding? Dann los! 🤝

Qualifikation

- Mehrjährige, nachweisbare Erfahrung im Performance Marketing, am besten im E-Commerce/D2C. Du nennst uns Zahlen, wir keine Ausreden.

- Sicherer Umgang mit Media Buying auf Meta, Funnels, Advertorials, Offer-Creation und KPIs aus eigener Praxis, nicht nur aus Kursen

- Keine Angst vor Zahlen: Du hast bereits hohe Werbebudgets eigenverantwortlich gesteuert.

- Führungserfahrung , oder klar belegbar, dass du ein Team aufbauen und führen kannst

- Hohe Eigenverantwortung, Tempo und Entscheidungsstärke: Du wartest nicht auf Anweisungen

- Du packst selbst an, wo es nötig ist, und scheust Arbeit nicht

- Von Vorteil: Shopify, JTL-Warenwirtschaft, Adobe Premiere/Illustrator/Photoshop und Erfahrung im Nageldesign-Bereich

Das ist nichts für dich, wenn du auf Ausbildung oder Anleitung wartest, einen ruhigen Job mit festen Feierabendzeiten suchst oder Ergebnisse lieber erklärst, als sie zu liefern.

Das ist genau dein Ding, wenn du Zahlen liebst, ein Team führen und mit ihm gewinnen willst und sagst: „Gebt mir Verantwortung und Freiraum, ich liefere.“

Benefits

- Erfolgsabhängige Vergütung ohne Limit: Wir messen unser Marketing sauber. Du wirst direkt an dem beteiligt, was du erreichst. Je mehr du bewegst, desto mehr verdienst du. Als Angestellte:r mit Fixgehalt plus Beteiligung, als Freelancer mit Honorar plus Beteiligung.

- Volle Verantwortung: Hauptverantwortliche:r für Marketing, mit Entscheidungsfreiheit über Strategie, Kanäle und Budget und deinem eigenen Team

- Ein Umfeld für Macher:innen: Hohes Tempo, kurze Entscheidungswege, direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung. Wir testen, messen und skalieren, statt zu diskutieren.

- Leistung zählt: Ergebnisse stehen im Mittelpunkt. Wer liefert, bekommt mehr Verantwortung.

- Hohe Erwartungen, klare Ziele: Wir wollen schnell wachsen und erwarten vollen Einsatz, auch dann, wenn es mal Launches, Aktionen oder Wochenenden verlangen.

- Flexibel, wo es geht: Ortsunabhängig, Home-Office oder Büro vor Ort. Wo und wann du arbeitest, entscheidest du, solange das Ergebnis stimmt.

- Faire Basis mit 30 Urlaubstagen (bei Festanstellung)

- Ein junges Team mit flachen Hierarchien

- Eine große Mission: Du baust mit uns eine der stärksten Marken im Nageldesign-Online-Handel auf

Wir freuen uns, mit dir zu arbeiten! Let's goooo! 🚀

title: Senior Rust Developer
description:
About Workato 

Workato is the leading Control and Execution Platform for Enterprise AI — the neutral platform enterprises trust to put AI to work across their business. Workato unifies data, applications, and processes into a single platform so AI can reliably orchestrate business processes in production at enterprise scale. Built on more than a decade of running mission-critical processes for over half the Fortune 500 — including Nasdaq, Amazon, Cisco, Vodafone, Atlassian, and Lucid Motors — Workato turns over 14,000 enterprise systems AI needs to act on into one governed execution layer. For more information, visit workato.com . 

Why join us? 

Ultimately, Workato believes in fostering a flexible, trust-oriented culture that empowers everyone to take full ownership of their roles . We are driven by innovation and looking for team players who want to actively build our company. 

But, we also believe in balancing productivity with self-care . That’s why we offer all of our employees a vibrant and dynamic work environment along with a multitude of benefits they can enjoy inside and outside of their work lives. 

If this sounds right up your alley, please submit an application. We look forward to getting to know you! 

Also, feel free to check out why: 

- Business Insider named us an “enterprise startup to bet your career on” 

- Forbes’ Cloud 100 recognized us as one of the top 100 private cloud companies in the world 

- Deloitte Tech Fast 500 ranked us as the 17th fastest growing tech company in the Bay Area, and 96th in North America 

- Quartz ranked us the #1 best company for remote workers 

Responsibilities 

We are looking for a Senior Rust Software Developer. In this role, y ou will also be responsible to: 

- 
Building new products inside the company.

- 
Develop new code with Rust, and deal with existing Go/Ruby code

- 
Create PoC in the new areas and drive them to production or drop them away.

Requirements 

Qualifications / Experience / Technical Skills 

- Strong experience writing, shipping, and maintaining Rust code (2+ years), and experience with other languages (Ruby, Python, Go, JS, Java, etc.)

- Knowledge of basic data structures and algorithms, multiprocessing, memory management.

- Experience developing high-performance asynchronous applications with Rust (preferably tokio).

- Good understanding of network protocols and stacks.

- Good understanding of DB technologies: classic databases and modern no-SQL.

- Basic knowledge of DevOps practices and tools

- Understanding of Linux environment

- Golang/Ruby knowledge is a plus

- Experience working with WASM is a plus

- Open Source contributions is a plus

Soft Skills / Personal Characteristics 

- Readiness to work remotely with teams distributed across the world and timezones

- Spoken English (at the level enough to pass the technical interview and later work with colleagues)

- Being a result-oriented problem solver.

- Prefers coming up with proposals in problematic areas, rather than being passive.

- Being open to new technologies and switching between projects.

- Readiness to travel for business

description:
Als Senior Sales Operations Manager – Compensation & Planning (m/w/d) verantwortest du die variable Vertriebsvergütung und den Budgetprozess für Deutschland. Darüber hinaus unterstützt du die übergreifende Vertriebssteuerung und das Reporting. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Vertriebsleitung, Finance und Analytics verbindest du technisches Know-how mit unternehmerischem Urteilsvermögen, um zuverlässige Abläufe und fundierte Geschäftsentscheidungen zu ermöglichen.

In dieser Rolle arbeitest du operativ, übernimmst viel Eigenverantwortung und stehst im direkten Austausch mit Führungskräften. Du arbeitest unmittelbar mit Daten und Systemen, entwickelst Handlungsempfehlungen und hinterfragst Annahmen konstruktiv.

Deine Aufgaben 

- 
Verantwortung für die variable Vertriebsvergütung übernehmen: Du steuerst den gesamten Prozess – von der Übersetzung vereinbarter Vergütungsmodelle in Berechnungslogiken über die Validierung der Ergebnisse und die Bereitstellung der Auszahlungsdaten bis zur Klärung von Rückfragen.

- 
Berechnungen und Reporting pflegen: Du schreibst SQL-Abfragen und passt Berechnungslogiken und Reports in QuickSuite an, wenn sich Ziele, Vertriebsstrukturen oder Vergütungsmodelle ändern. Du machst die Ergebnisse für die Vertriebsteams zugänglich und verständlich.

Eine zuverlässige Abwicklung sicherstellen: Du koordinierst die Aktualisierung unterschiedlicher Vertriebsziele sowie die Verarbeitung von Ausnahmen und manuellen Eingaben. Dabei sorgst du über die monatlichen und quartalsweisen Abrechnungszyklen hinweg für eine nachvollziehbare Dokumentation und wirksame Kontrollen.

- 
Den Budgetprozess für Deutschland verantworten: Du koordinierst die Planung mit Finance und den relevanten Fachbereichen, erstellst detaillierte Excel-Modelle, hinterfragst Annahmen und entwickelst Szenarien, die Risiken und Zielkonflikte transparent machen.

- 
Die Vertriebssteuerung unterstützen: Du analysierst die Vertriebsleistung und geschäftliche Einflussfaktoren, pflegst relevante Reports und leitest daraus Handlungsempfehlungen für die Vertriebsleitung ab.

- 
Mit Führungskräften und zentralen Stakeholdern zusammenarbeiten: Du entwickelst ein tiefes Verständnis unserer Vertriebsprozesse, bewertest Anfragen und bringst dich als konstruktiver Sparringspartner ein.

- 
Prozesse verbessern: Du erhöhst die Datenqualität, automatisierst wiederkehrende Aufgaben und steuerst konkurrierende Fristen vorausschauend – insbesondere während der Budgetplanung und rund um Quartalswechsel.

Das bringst du mit 

- 
Mindestens fünf Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung in Sales Operations, Vertriebssteuerung, variabler Vertriebsvergütung, Commercial Finance, Unternehmensplanung oder einer vergleichbaren analytischen Funktion.

- 
Sehr gute praktische SQL-Kenntnisse, Erfahrung mit QuickSuite oder vergleichbaren BI-Tools sowie fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse in der Excel-Modellierung. Du kannst Berechnungen und Reports eigenständig aufbauen, pflegen und Fehler darin beheben.

- 
Ein fundiertes Verständnis von Vertriebsprozessen, wirtschaftlichen Erfolgsfaktoren und Anreizmechanismen sowie die Neugier, unser Geschäft im Detail kennenzulernen.

- 
Gutes unternehmerisches Urteilsvermögen und die Sicherheit, eine eigene Position zu entwickeln, Annahmen konstruktiv zu hinterfragen und mit Führungskräften souverän zusammenzuarbeiten.

- 
Ein hohes Maß an Eigenverantwortung, eine sorgfältige Arbeitsweise und die Fähigkeit, Prioritäten zu setzen und auch in arbeitsintensiven Phasen zuverlässig Ergebnisse zu liefern.

- 
Fließende Englischkenntnisse und Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens B2-Niveau. Du kannst Fragen zur variablen Vergütung direkt mit deutschsprachigen Vertriebskollegen besprechen.

title: Senior Technical Support Specialist (m/f/x)
description:
About Commercetools

Real innovation starts with a strong foundation, and at commercetools, that comes from the perfect balance of our product and our people. Behind every leap forward is a collective of builders, explorers, doers, makers, and problem-solvers. The kind of people who not only pioneered a more flexible approach to commerce architecture but also shaped the culture of experimentation that approach unlocked. Together they are the engine of commerce innovation today. At commercetools, we power the next era of commerce for our customers. Whether it’s AI-driven solutions that help enterprises make smarter business decisions, bridging digital and physical shopping experiences, or enabling entirely new ways for industries to connect with their customers, we help the world’s most ambitious companies experiment, scale, and grow without limits. Here the best idea wins, not the loudest voice. You will have the tools, trust, and space to not only build the future of commerce, but to build your own.

Your Impact

Location: Munich, Germany (Hybrid: 3 days/week in-office)

Team: IT and Security Operations

As a Technical Support Specialist on the IT and Security Operations Team, you will serve as a responsive problem solver and technical subject-matter expert for our colleagues, in support of security operations, and as a collaborative member of a global team. This includes having a sharp focus on responsive communications, ownership, and advanced technical knowledge.

You will: 

- Global & Local IT Support: Provide responsive, senior-tier technical support and ITSM for employees in Munich and globally. Act as the escalation point for highly complex technical issues and suspected security concerns.

- Employee Lifecycle & Device Management: Ensure seamless employee onboarding and offboarding. Manage and configure Apple laptops (macOS) and mobile devices (iOS) using tools like Jamf.

- Security & Incident Response: Partner with security leadership to expand our Information Security Management System (ISMS). Manage endpoint security and vulnerability solutions (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon EDR, Zscaler). Lead incident response, containment, and root cause analysis.

- Identity & Access Management (IAM): Oversee IAM operations (e.g., Okta), including access requests, cloud integrations, proactive remediation, and auditing to ensure adherence to least-privilege principles.

- Network Strategy: Support and optimize local area networks (LAN) and office Wi-Fi (UniFi devices), focusing on stability, performance, and capacity planning.

- Strategy & Leadership: Architect disaster-recovery processes for core IAM systems. Design compliance reporting structures. Mentor peers, share best practices, and lead cross-functional technical initiatives.

What Sets You Apart

You're a creative problem-solver who is wired to find solutions. You confidently dive into complex challenges and have a talent for making them simple for others. Your curiosity drives you to constantly grow and contribute to an environment of trust and teamwork. Great ideas come from many paths, and your unique perspective matters more than checking every box. What matters most is the mindset you bring to the work.

You bring: 

- Language Skills: Fully fluent in both German and English (written and spoken). 

- Technical Expertise: Advanced knowledge of supporting and managing Apple environments (macOS/iOS) and cloud-native/SaaS services.

- Security & IAM: Direct experience with endpoint security platforms (Zscaler, CrowdStrike Falcon EDR) and Identity and Access Management solutions (e.g., Okta).

- Network Experience: Proven ability configuring and managing office Wi-Fi and LAN infrastructure.

- Project & Stakeholder Leadership: Track record of leading operational initiatives, change management, and representing IT in cross-departmental discussions. Ability to translate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

- Pacing & Adaptability: Comfortable juggling multiple initiatives and reprioritizing in a high-velocity environment without compromising service quality.

- Culture Add: A collaborative mindset that cultivates belonging, seeks feedback, and actively participates in company culture.

AI Aptitude: A genuine curiosity for using AI tools to work smarter and more effectively, paired with a drive to learn and put them into practice in your role.

Nice to Have: 

- Okta and/or Jamf Administration

- Atlassian Cloud, Confluence and Jira

- IT Asset Management (ITAM), Inventory Management

- IT and/or Security Certifications

- Bug Bounty Programs

- Security CTFs, threat hunting, SOC (Security Operations Center)

Our Benefits 

Because work and life are connected, our benefits are too. We’ve designed them to give you the security, flexibility, and opportunities you need to focus on what matters most.

🩺 Comprehensive health benefits for you and your dependents, including access to OpenUp for personalized mental health support

📚 Learning and development opportunities including an annual learning budget, access to self-paced learning platforms and language training, personalized coaching, mentorship, and leadership programs

🍼 Family Leave Plus gives you additional fully paid weeks of parental leave on top of government-provided leave, so you can spend more time with your new addition

📈 Our equity participation program allows you to share in our success 

For more information on our benefits, visit this page. 

Come as you are. Build with us. 

Your unique perspective is essential to our success. We are committed to building a team that reflects the world around us because we know it’s the only way to build the future. We celebrate our differences and have created a hiring process that’s fair, inclusive, and designed to let your talent shine.

title: Technical Business Development Intern (Emerging Verticals) (f/m/d)
description:
Description 

QuantumDiamonds is building the world's first commercial quantum sensing tools for chip failure analysis. Our Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDm) images magnetic fields with micrometer resolution, and that capability could matter far beyond semiconductors. As our Technical Business Development Intern for Emerging Verticals in the Data Science & Machine Learning team in Pre-Development, you help us find out where.

Working directly with our project lead for Emerging Verticals, who mentors you, you explore new application fields for widefield magnetic imaging. You dig into the science and the markets behind them, talk to potential customers and users, and help turn promising ideas into first feasibility studies with our magnetic field imaging system. You see how a deep tech company decides where its technology goes next, and help shape that decision.

This is a full-time internship for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

Who we are 

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join Quantum Diamonds? 

Picture this: 

- Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

- Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

- Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

- An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us? 

- You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

- From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

- Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

- You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible! 

What will you do 

- Map and evaluate application areas for magnetic field imaging beyond semiconductors: key players, customer segments and structured comparisons of use cases.

- Review scientific literature and patents to understand the state of the art, competing measurement methods, and where NV-based imaging offers a real advantage.

- Prepare and join discovery conversations with researchers and companies to understand their measurement challenges, and keep contacts and opportunities up to date in our CRM.

- Support feasibility studies with our experts, from defining suitable samples to interpreting first measurement results.

- Turn your findings into clear deliverables such as application one-pagers, decision memos, and presentations.

What is expected of you 

- Enrolled in or recently graduated from a degree program in physics, engineering, materials science, chemistry, biophysics, or a related natural science or engineering field, ideally with some Python exposure.

- Available full time for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

- Curiosity about how a new measurement technology can solve problems in fields you may not know yet.

- Clear writing and structured analysis: you turn a pile of papers and conversations into a one-page recommendation.

- AI tools are part of how you research, analyze and write, and you check their output the way you check your own.

- Fluent in English. On-site in Munich.

Business studies or first experience in market research, consulting, or a startup is a plus, not required.

Our benefits 

- Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

- Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

- Mentoring: An experienced colleague from the team mentors you throughout your internship.

- Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

- Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

- Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 24 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

About us 

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

The Platform Operations Director should be able to identify operational risks early, challenge whether a solution is genuinely ready for release, and recommend practical improvements to processes, documentation, testing, support models and stakeholder communications.

3. Business Readiness and Adoption

4. Release Readiness and Service Transition 

- Own or coordinate release readiness checklists for assigned solutions.

- Ensure each release has appropriate testing evidence, documentation, support ownership, training material and stakeholder communication.

- Coordinate operational handover from delivery teams into BAU support.

- Confirm that runbooks, troubleshooting guides, known issues and escalation routes are in place.

- Work with engineering and data teams to ensure monitoring, alerting or manual checks are defined where required.

- Support go-live planning, release scheduling and post-release hypercare.

“Are we actually ready to put this live, support it, explain it, and measure whether it worked?”

5. Documentation and Knowledge Management

6. Platform and Process Governance

description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The role 

We’re looking for a GTM Operations Manager to build and improve the workflows that connect our go-to-market teams.

A promising account signs up. Does the right person find out, with enough context to act? A customer becomes eligible for a new product. Do they receive useful guidance? A data sync fails overnight. Do we catch it before it affects a campaign, account handoff, or business decision?

You’ll help make those things work reliably.

You’ll join an existing GTM Operations team, working closely with @Nathan Bellehsen on Salesforce and Sales systems and @Masha Tsaryk on Marketing and customer-lifecycle systems. Your initial focus will be lead handoffs and lifecycle execution: the data, automation, quality checks, and reporting that turn customer signals into useful action.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role. You’ll own agreed projects from understanding the problem through building, testing, rollout, and ongoing improvement. Experienced teammates will provide context, help set priorities, and partner with you on architectural decisions. Within that direction, we expect you to make progress independently and flag problems early.

Our stack includes Salesforce, Customer.io , Clay, Looker, automation tools, and a growing set of AI workflows. You don’t need to know every tool. You do need to understand how systems connect and enjoy figuring out why something isn’t working.

Why we’re hiring for this role now 

RevenueCat’s GTM organization is growing across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Growth. We’re developing more deliberate ways to identify promising accounts, help customers adopt our products, and turn successful one-to-one work into programs that reach many more people.

Our operations team already supports the systems behind that work. We need more capacity to take important workflows from “this could work” to something dependable that people use every day.

You’ll help us ship those improvements while making the existing operation easier to run: fewer manual handoffs, clearer ownership, more trustworthy data, and less time spent solving the same problem twice.

What you’ll be responsible for 

- Own selected GTM workflows end-to-end. Translate a business problem into a practical solution, agree how success will be measured, build and test it, and stay responsible after launch.

- Make lead and account handoffs dependable. Build and improve enrichment, qualification, routing, alerts, and follow-up visibility. Help ensure important signals reach a named owner, and make missed or failed handoffs visible.

- Put lifecycle programs into production. Partner with Marketing and Customer Growth on audience definitions, triggers, exclusions, data syncs, campaign QA, and measurement. Turn repeatable requests into workflows and templates teammates can use.

- Keep data connected and usable. Trace how account, contact, and product-usage data moves between systems. Investigate stale records, duplicates, mismatched relationships, and failed syncs; fix what you can and work with the relevant system or Data owner on deeper issues.

- Build automation that holds up in everyday use. Test realistic scenarios and edge cases, monitor failures, and make it clear how to recover when something breaks. Bring consequential changes to the relevant system owner before rollout.

- Use AI where it improves the work. Build or improve workflows for tasks such as enrichment, research, qualification, and quality checks. Evaluate the output, understand the failure modes, and measure whether the result saves time or improves quality.

- Make what you build understandable and useful. Document your workflows, enable the people using them, gather feedback, and improve adoption. Share knowledge so another teammate can operate and troubleshoot your work. Keep documentation current as workflows change, and fill gaps in the existing processes you take on.

- Make operational performance visible. Build and maintain reports that help teams understand workflow health, handoff gaps, campaign execution, and adoption. Work with senior Ops teammates and Data on consistent definitions.

What you’ll need to be successful 

- 3+ years of hands-on experience in GTM, revenue, marketing, sales, or customer operations.

- Practical Salesforce experience. You understand objects, relationships, fields, flows, and how data moves through the system. You have built or changed things yourself.

- Experience building in a marketing automation platform such as Customer.io , HubSpot, Marketo, Braze, or Iterable, including segmentation, triggers, and integrations.

- Experience building something useful with AI. You can explain the problem, your contribution, how you checked the result, what failed, and what you changed. A sanitized walkthrough is welcome; we don’t expect confidential work from a previous employer.

- Ownership and follow-through. You can take an agreed problem, work through ambiguity, communicate tradeoffs, and deliver without needing every step assigned.

- Care for the details. You think about the wrong audience, missing record, duplicate trigger, or failed handoff before it becomes someone else’s problem.

Ideally, you 

- Have worked in a product-led or usage-based business with both self-service and Sales-assisted customers.

- Have connected CRM, marketing automation, customer-success, or product-usage systems.

- Can use SQL, APIs, webhooks, or lightweight scripts to investigate data and connect tools.

- Have improved adoption of an internal tool or replaced repeated manual work with a maintained workflow.

- Have supported customer onboarding, product adoption, lifecycle education, or account-coverage programs.

What success looks like

title: Corporate Development Director
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 

An overview of this role

As the Corporate Development Director, you'll help influence how GitLab invests to win: what we build, what we buy, where we partner, and what we should not pursue. This role sits within the Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships.

This role straddles strategy and M&A engagements. You'll lead research that frames GitLab's options: mapping the markets in and around our AI-powered DevSecOps platform, testing where we have a right to win, and turning that into clear recommendations for the executive team. When the answer is to acquire, you'll drive the deal process end to end, from outreach through close and integration.

Success here is not measured by deal count. It looks like sharper strategic choices: a well-reasoned point of view on our priority markets, investment theses that product and executive leaders rely on, acquisitions that speed up the roadmap when buying is the right answer, and an educated no when it isn't. You'll own the wider market perspective rather than individual product categories, and work with the team's Analyst on the research behind it.

What you'll do

Strategy and research

- Own the wider market view. Research the broader market GitLab competes in, beyond specific product categories: competitive dynamics, AI-native entrants, technology shifts and where value is moving. Collaborate with the team's Analyst on the research and turn the findings into a clear point of view on where GitLab should play.

- Build an investment thesis for each focus area. Work with Product and Engineering leaders to define the problems worth solving, the capabilities GitLab needs, and what it would cost in time and money to get there on our own.

- Own the competitive and landscape view. Maintain market maps and a current read on GitLab's competitors: their strategy, product direction, positioning, pricing, and M&A and funding activity. Produce competitor analyses that show where we lead, where we're exposed and how rivals are likely to move. Flag shifts by competitors, hyperscalers and AI labs that change our options, and bring the implications to Product and the executive team.

- Define where GitLab should not play. Identify adjacencies that dilute focus and markets where the economics or competition work against us. Make the case for a no with the same rigor as a yes.

Build, buy or partner

- Run the build, buy, partner analysis. For each strategic gap, compare the options side by side on speed, cost, risk, control and strategic fit, and bring a clear recommendation.

- Deliver strategic clarity to executives and the Board. Produce short strategy memos/decks and business cases that set out the decision, the trade-offs and what we give up with each path.

- Feed company strategy and planning. Bring an outside-in view of the market and the inorganic options available into annual and long-range planning.

- Work hand in hand with Strategic Partnerships. When partnering is the right answer, frame the opportunity and hand it to the partnership owner with a clear thesis. When it isn't, explain why.

Deal execution and integration

- Own end-to-end deal process management. Validate target fit against GitLab's our target profile, product roadmap and other criteria, and build the acquisition rationale and business case. Drive our M&A process from intro call through the various steps through to closing and integration.

- Evaluate the deal. Develop valuation, commercial integrity assessment, impact on GitLab's business and provide negotiations assistance to the VP and the executive team.

- Lead cross-functional diligence. Run pre-LOI validation and diligence across Product, Engineering, Security, Finance, Legal and People, and communicate findings clearly.

- Drive deal documents with Legal. Prepare NDAs, LOIs and purchase agreements with GitLab Legal and outside counsel.

- Own integration outcomes. Lead post-acquisition integration as the DRI, measured against the roadmap and business goals in the business case. Bring lessons learned back into the strategy work.

- Build the external network. Maintain relationships with founders, executives, investors, bankers and advisors that bring us early insight and pipeline.

What you'll bring

- Strategy and deal experience. 8+ years across corporate development, corporate strategy, strategy consulting or technology investing, including 5+ years leading acquisitions end to end in enterprise software.

- Structured strategic thinking. You form a point of view from incomplete information, test it against data, and change your mind when the evidence says so. You're as comfortable recommending that we stay out of a market as that we enter it.

- Market research depth. Skilled in market sizing, competitive analysis and landscape mapping, and in turning research into a recommendation, not a report.

- Deal craft. Skilled in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, negotiation and integration planning, with experience across varied consideration structures.

- Technical fluency. A working understanding of software development, DevSecOps and the AI landscape, enough to hold substantive conversations with product and engineering leaders about roadmaps and architecture.

- Clear executive communication. You write short, decision-ready updates and present trade-offs plainly to executives and the Board, in an async-first environment.

- Influence without authority. You build trust across Product, Engineering, Finance and Legal and move decisions forward across functions.

- Ownership with collaboration. You own the strategic view and the recommendation, and partner closely with the team's Analyst on research and analysis.

- Preferred: familiarity with the DevSecOps, security, AI and open source ecosystems.

- You value the all remote lifestyle and share our values .

About the team

The Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team helps GitLab decide how to grow beyond what we build on our own. We own inorganic strategy: acquisitions, strategic partnerships with hyperscalers and AI labs, and the research that tells us which to pursue and which to pass on.

We work across Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal and the executive group. We set direction and do the detailed work ourselves, with a high degree of ownership and transparency in a fully remote, asynchronous environment.

description:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance .

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. 

Location: Oxford, England, UK
Working pattern: Hybrid

Role: 

We are looking for a Senior Silicon Validation Engineer to join our Cryo-CMOS IC team at IonQ Oxford. You will lead the validation and characterisation of analogue and mixed-signal ASICs for our trapped-ion quantum processors, from test planning and platform development through first-silicon bring-up, debug and system integration.

This is a hands-on technical role. You will shape our validation architecture, build reusable hardware and software, and provide the evidence needed to make confident silicon acceptance decisions. The work includes room-temperature silicon validation and silicon characterisation at cryogenic temperatures (around 4 kelvin), on packaged parts, chip-on-board assemblies and bare die on a cryogenic probe station.

Responsibilities: 

You will own validation delivery across chip and system interfaces, working closely with analogue and digital design, verification, modelling, firmware and systems engineers. You will turn requirements into measurable tests, prepare platforms before silicon arrives and resolve failures across the chip, board and software.

As a Senior engineer, you will set technical standards, guide other engineers and improve coverage, repeatability and test efficiency across successive ASIC generations.

Key responsibilities include:

- 
Own the silicon validation strategy, plans, acceptance criteria and readiness reviews, with traceability from block and system requirements to tests, results and unresolved risks.

- 
Present the silicon acceptance report to the Cryo-CMOS IC Lead and programme stakeholders.

- 
Lead first-silicon bring-up and characterisation of sample-and-hold and switch arrays, DACs, ADCs, references, amplifiers, switches, regulators, clocking and device-level test structures, across supply, temperature, operating modes and device variation, with sound calibration and measurement uncertainty.

- 
Develop validation boards, fixtures and reusable Python automation, instrument drivers and regression suites, addressing signal integrity, grounding, power integrity and measurement access, with version-controlled tests and reproducible data analysis.

- 
Plan and lead cryogenic measurements with specialist colleagues, including bare-die probing and the cold signal chain, and drive failures to root cause, separating silicon defects from board, firmware and test artefacts and correlating results with simulations, device models and foundry or partner data.

- 
Influence testability before tape-out, coordinate validation with external design partners, the foundry and other IonQ sites.

- 
Lead technical reviews, mentor engineers and document methods to improve throughput, data quality and reuse.

Requirements: 

You will bring substantial experience in analogue or mixed-signal silicon validation and characterisation, with ownership of multiple silicon bring-up programmes. A degree in electrical or electronic engineering, or equivalent practical experience, is expected. You should combine hands-on laboratory skills with sound judgement on test coverage, measurement confidence and programme risk.

You’d be a great fit with:

- 
Strong electronics fundamentals and experience validating precision signal chains, data converters or power-management circuits, including their digital control interfaces.

- 
Practical expertise with oscilloscopes, precision sources and meters, signal generators, spectrum and logic analysers; confidence designing reliable low-noise, low-leakage measurements.

- 
Strong Python programming for instrument control, automated testing and statistical analysis; disciplined use of Git or equivalent version control and maintainable test software.

- 
Experience designing and debugging test PCBs, reviewing layouts and working with interfaces such as SPI, I2C, JTAG and custom shift-register chains, alongside embedded firmware or FPGA-based platforms.

- 
A record of resolving complex chip, board and software interactions through structured experiments and collaboration.

- 
Experience leading technical projects, mentoring engineers and communicating evidence, uncertainty and decisions in clear written reports.

Useful additional experience includes cryogenic or other extreme-temperature testing; wafer or bare-die probing; early-stage IP or test-chip evaluation; FPGA development and C/C++; circuit simulation; and production test correlation. Prior quantum computing is welcome but not required.

Benefits: 

Be part of a team that’s shaping the future of quantum. We offer more than just a role, you’ll join a world class community of scientists, engineers and innovators working to unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

We offer a range of benefits, including opportunities to further your career alongside industry leaders, a competitive salary with IonQ stock options, an annual performance bonus, generous annual leave, flexible hybrid working, private medical and dental insurance for you and your family, and much more.

Join us and be part of the future of quantum computing.

- Experience in a customer-facing role such as Customer Success or Account Management — ideally supporting a data, intelligence, or SaaS product.

- Comfortable using AI and automation tools in your day-to-day work, and curious to find smarter ways of doing things.

- Analytical and process-minded — you like understanding what drives client value.

- Proactive and comfortable with ambiguity — happy to figure things out and get stuck in.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable 

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning. 

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission 

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not. 

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem 

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to. 

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you. 

If it's on you, it's in your control. 

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift 

Honesty is an expression of care. 

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

title: Fraud Risk Manager
description:
About Aspora 

People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.

Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. About the Role 

People build lives across borders, and their money should move with them. Every product, corridor and payment rail we add opens a new door for fraudsters. We want to be the least attractive target on our corridors, without adding friction for good customers. This role exists to own how we detect and deter fraud across every rail and geo.

You’ll lead fraud detection and deterrence end to end, from exposure mapping to rules, limits and customer protection. You report to our Head of Financial Crime and work alongside the fraud recovery and chargebacks lead. You partner with Product, Payments, Engineering, Customer Support and Compliance on every launch. You decide what ships on day one, and you own the trade-off between fraud caught and friction added.

Who You Are 

You don’t see fraud as a dashboard to watch. You see it as a live contest, won or lost in seconds, and you’ve been in it.

- You’ve done multiple rodeos. You’ve worked fraud at more than one fintech or high-velocity regulated platform across the UK, EU or US. That could be a neobank, payments company, gambling operator, gaming platform or crypto exchange. You know how attacks, rails and rules differ in each.

- You’ve built controls from scratch. At a B2C fintech, you built fraud controls that didn’t exist before, while protecting consumer money at scale.

- You’ve worked the floor. You started as an investigator and worked alerts and cases by hand. You spot a pattern before it shows on a dashboard.

- You’ve been baptised by fire. You’ve handled a real fraud attack or loss spike and made fast calls under pressure. You stayed on it until the fix held, and learned from every case.

- You own the approach. You decide how to tackle a problem and see it through end to end, without waiting to be told.

- You see every launch as a new door. You map where fraud can get in before go-live, not after the first losses land.

- You protect good customers too. You stop fraud without adding friction for the people we serve, and you can show the numbers behind it.

Most importantly, you’d rather build the right controls once, on our own decisioning platform, than tune vendor defaults forever.

What You’ll Own 

This is a role with a mandate across every rail, product and geo we operate in.

- See the exposure, everywhere. Map where fraud can hit us on every rail, product and geo, and own the observability layer that lets us watch it live.

- Build rules that hold. Stand up rule building and governance on our decisioning platform, with every change back-tested before it ships.

- Tier exposure by risk. Design progressive access to payment rails by risk tier, so trusted customers move freely and limits grow with trust.

- Measure every trade-off. Track each control change in fraud caught against friction added, and retire the rules that no longer earn their place.

- Protect customers in the moment. Put vulnerable-customer education and in-the-moment verification on every rail, without slowing good customers down.

- Launch with controls from day one. Make sure every new product, geo or rail has a signed-off exposure map before it goes live.

Your calls will shape how fast Aspora can open new corridors, and how safely customers move money once we’re there.

Why Aspora 

- Define how Aspora detects and deters fraud across every rail and geo, and set the playbook every launch follows.

- Work directly with our Head of Financial Crime, and partner with Product, Payments and Engineering on every launch.

- Build controls on our own decisioning platform, across high-volume cross-border flows at significant scale.

- Own fraud strategy from day one, from exposure mapping through to customer protection.

- Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora’s long-term vision.

About Aspora 

People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.

Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.

We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.

About the Role 

People build lives across borders, and their finances should move with them. We’re building Aspora for the global diaspora, starting with Indians abroad. Regulation sits at the centre of that ambition. This role exists to turn a complex set of requirements into a practical way to build and run the business. One global framework, local differences only where the law needs them, and decisions made by clear frameworks rather than daily escalations.

You’ll lead licensing, regulator engagement, product advice, safeguarding oversight, customer protection and operational resilience. You’ll report to our COO, working alongside our Global MLRO. You’ll partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance and local compliance owners to turn requirements into working controls. You’ll own the regulatory calls on launches, changes and the commitments we make to regulators.

Who You Are 

You don’t see regulation as a reason to say no, or as something to work around. You know a hard boundary from a choice, and your depth goes well beyond AML or licensing paperwork.

- You’ve scaled fintechs before. You’ve helped a payments, remittance or e-money business grow, in house or as a consultant, and can show what you changed.

- You turn expertise into execution. You’ve translated payments and e-money requirements into customer journeys, controls and processes, with fewer failures and less friction to show for it.

- You get permissions over the line. You’ve owned licensing or variation work and regulatory reporting, and kept applications, governance and operating reality consistent throughout.

- You speak regulator fluently, and you’ve been tested. You’ve handled supervisory questions, inspections or a hard remediation, made sound calls under pressure and stayed until it was fixed.

- You’ve set standards at HQ level. You’ve built shared standards across markets and distributed teams, and you know where local law needs a difference and where duplication is habit.

- You’ve seen controls work in practice. You go deep on UK payments, e-money, safeguarding and customer protection, and you’ve followed gaps through to a verified fix.

- You’re on the way up. Your career shows quick progression, growing ownership and real depth. We’ll judge the work you’ve done, not the title you hold.

Most importantly, you want to build a global regulatory framework from the ground up and see it work in practice.

What You’ll Own 

This is a role with a genuinely global mandate, with UK payments and e-money regulation as the depth anchor.

- Own licensing and regulator engagement. Lead permissions, perimeter analysis, applications and variations, with accurate filings and a clear register of every commitment we make.

- Shape products before they launch. Assess launches and changes against UK PSRs, EMRs and FCA rules, and turn horizon scanning into owned implementation plans.

- Hold safeguarding to a high standard. Challenge the design, test the evidence and keep us audit ready, partnering with Finance on reconciliations and governance.

- Make customer protection measurable. Drive Consumer Duty, fair value, vulnerable customers, complaints and partner oversight, using outcome data to spot harm and assign action.

- Own the regulatory view on resilience. Partner with operations and technology owners on service mapping, testing and outsourcing oversight, and own the incident reporting decisions.

- Build one global framework. Set shared standards across markets, add local differences only where law requires them, and bring in local expertise where it’s needed.

What you build here will shape where Aspora can launch, how quickly we get there, and how much regulators trust us along the way.

Why Aspora 

- Define the global regulatory compliance framework for a borderless financial platform, from first principles.

- Work directly with our COO and Global MLRO, and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance and Operations.

- Set the standard for how a regulated fintech scales across multiple jurisdictions without losing pace.

- Own licensing, product advice, safeguarding oversight and customer protection from day one, not a narrow slice of compliance.

- Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora’s long-term vision.

title: Senior Recruiter | GTM Expansion
description:
About Ramp 

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role 

At Ramp, people are the single biggest lever on our trajectory, and the bar for who joins this team gets higher every quarter, not lower. We are hiring our first dedicated Recruiter for GTM Expansion, based in London: someone who can map a market, identify the operators who will outperform their peers and run a full-cycle process that wins them.

The UK is the immediate mandate. You will partner with local and US-based leaders to turn an ambitious growth plan into a real commercial team, from first conversation through offer close. You will also help us build the recruiting approach, market knowledge and candidate networks that support Ramp's expansion into new GTM markets over time.

The recruiters who do this best combine craft on the front end, research, identification and calibration, with execution on the back end, closing, candidate experience and pipeline discipline. We are looking for both.

What You'll Do 

• Own full-cycle recruiting for priority GTM Expansion hiring, starting with UK roles across Sales, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships and Customer Success.

• Build a sharp point of view on the UK market and future expansion markets: the companies producing strong talent, the people who outperform their peers and the communities that matter.

• Use research, data and AI as part of your everyday craft to identify and qualify exceptional candidates. We expect a written market point of view, not just a slate of profiles.

• Run thoughtful, personalised outreach grounded in the candidate's actual background, commercial motion or recent work. We care more about quality, replies and conversion than send volume.

• Partner with GTM leaders to turn ambitious hiring plans into a clear profile, credible process and realistic compensation strategy. Surface hard market truth early and push back constructively when needed.

• Own the candidate experience from first conversation through offer close: fast follow-up, clear communication, strong process discipline and a tailored closing plan for the candidates we most want.

• Build real presence for Ramp in London through the right relationships, referrals and targeted community activity. The point is pipeline and credibility, not events for their own sake.

• Work tightly with the wider GTM Recruiting team on calibration, sourcing support, insight and operating rhythm, while bringing strong local judgment.

• Help improve how Ramp recruits for expansion by capturing what works in the UK and applying it thoughtfully as we enter new markets.

What You Need 

• 5+ years of full-cycle GTM or Sales recruiting experience, ideally in a high-growth technology company where quality and pace both mattered.

• Strong knowledge of the UK technology talent market and a credible local network, or clear evidence that you can build one quickly.

• A track record of finding and closing exceptional people, not simply running inherited processes. You can point to candidates you identified who became strong hires.

• Excellent sourcing and research instincts. You can explain why someone is genuinely differentiated, not only that they have the right title at the right company.

• Experience hiring across several GTM functions, such as AEs, Sales Leadership, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships, Customer Success or RevOps.

• Strong candidate-closing judgment. You listen closely, understand what each candidate is weighing and can build conviction against serious alternatives.

• The confidence to influence senior leaders, challenge a mis-scoped search and make a hiring process better without creating unnecessary friction.

• Comfort using data to understand funnel health, diagnose problems and hold an honest conversation about what needs to change.

• High ownership. You book the next step while you have the candidate, chase what is stuck and do not wait for a detailed brief to get useful work moving.

• Specific, sharp written communication. Your outreach and candidate updates should never feel template-driven.

Nice to Have 

• Experience recruiting for a fintech, SaaS, infrastructure or similarly complex B2B product.

• Experience joining a company as the first recruiter in a new geography, or helping to scale an international business.

• Experience building an AI-augmented recruiting research workflow.

Why this Role 

You will have unusual ownership over one of Ramp's most important growth priorities, with the support of an established Talent team rather than the isolation of a one-person recruiting function. The work is practical and high impact: build the UK commercial team, help leaders make better hiring decisions and raise the bar for how Ramp recruits as it enters new markets.

title: Team Lead Manager - Product Engineer
description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here .

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for highly technical engineers who want to lead and manage one of our engineering teams. It took over 10,000 interviews to hire our first 50 Omneans, and we’re now growing from 11 to more than 14 engineering teams in the coming months. Over the next year, our engineering team will double in size, our enterprise customer base will grow from ~180 to 300+, and revenue will triple.

As a Team Lead Manager, you’ll lead a small team of engineers. You’ll set its technical direction, line-manage and grow the people in it, and stay hands-on in the code. This is not a hands-off management role: our teams are small, and you’ll be one of the strongest engineers on yours. You’ll partner closely with a Product Manager and Product Designer to decide what to build, and you’ll be accountable for how well it’s built and how fast it ships.

If you’re a strong Tech Lead who hasn’t managed people yet, we’d still love to hear from you. You can start as a Team Lead, with management handled by an Engineering Manager, and grow into the full role with our support.

What Can You Expect As a Team Lead Manager?

- Lead and Manage a Small Team. Line-manage the engineers on your team, run 1:1s, give feedback, and help them take on bigger problems.

- Stay Deeply Technical. You’ll still build. Expect to spend a meaningful share of your time writing code, reviewing PRs, and unblocking the hardest technical problems.

- AI-Native Development. AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude, Code, and agentic workflows every day, and our product is built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows. You’ll set the bar for how your team uses them.

- Customers at the Center. Talk directly with customers to understand their problems, and make sure your team builds things that create real value for them.

- Own Technical Direction. Make the architecture and design calls for your team’s problem space, and own the trade-offs between speed, quality, and long-term maintainability.

- Work with Modern Technology. TypeScript across the stack, React, Postgres, and AWS serverless (Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge), managed through Pulumi and deployed via GitHub Actions. Datadog, Meticulous, and Incident.io round it out.

- Shape the Roadmap. Work with your PM and Designer on prioritisation, scoping, and sequencing so the team ships what matters most.

- Build the Team. Interview, hire, and onboard new engineers as we double in size.

About You

- You’re a highly technical full-stack engineer. You’ve designed and shipped web apps end to end in TypeScript, ideally on AWS serverless, and you’re still one of the strongest engineers in the room.

- You’ve led engineers. You’ve been a Tech Lead, Team Lead, or TLM, owning delivery and technical direction for a team.

- You want to manage people, or grow into it. Ideally, you’ve line-managed engineers already. If not, you’re keen to learn.

- You still love to build. Leading hasn’t pulled you away from the code, and you want a role where you keep shipping.

- You raise the bar. You know what well-architected, reliable software looks like, and you help others get there through reviews, pairing, and clear feedback.

- You’re motivated by customer impact. You care about outcomes for customers, not just output, and you make good calls on what to build and what to cut.

- You’re a strong partner. You work well with product and design, push back when it matters, and bring people with you.

- You’re comfortable with ambiguity. You can take an unclear problem, shape it, and get a team moving on it.

Nice-to-Haves

- You’ve led a team through fast growth, ideally at a scale-up where the team and product changed quickly.

- You’ve built B2B or enterprise SaaS, with complex workflows and demanding customers.

- You’ve performed exceptionally at something else, be it academics, sport, or work.

Interview Process

Before applying, we strongly encourage you to spend a few minutes in our R&D Candidate Hub. It covers our engineering culture, ways of working, interview process, tech environment, and what it’s like to build at Omnea.

R&D Candidate Hub : https://omnea.notion.site/R-D-Candidate-Hub-2f688cce658780f1b942c81cd3a032d4 

Note: our pair programming stage is in TypeScript OR Python and you’ll be assessed as if it’s your primary language. This is a full-stack, hands-on leadership role, so if you’re exclusively frontend, backend, or platform-focused, or no longer writing code, it likely isn’t the right fit.

The process generally includes:

- Initial screening call with our Talent team (30 mins, remote)

- AI Product Eng Challenge , language-agnostic (1 hour, remote)

- Onsite interviews at our Victoria office (~3 hours)

- Engineering Culture interview with an Engineering Manager or Team Lead (45 mins)

- System Design interview with a Senior Engineer (60 mins)

- Engineering Leadership interview with our CTO (45 mins)

- Office tour (15 mins)

We’re proud to support visa sponsorship for candidates who need it.

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

A few things to note: 

- We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here . 

- We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here 

- We're commercial, ambitious and we don't pretend otherwise! We're actively seeking folks looking to make the most of a career-defining opportunity, with the hunger to be part of building something really impressive . You can see our values here and our Omnea Future Founder's fund here !

- We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background).

We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow!

title: Medical Doctor with SNOMED Coding Experience (UK)
description:
We are seeking qualified medical doctors to annotate and code clinical documents with SNOMED CT, with a focus on accuracy and consistency against detailed coding guidelines.

You will work asynchronously on a dedicated annotation platform, coding de-identified clinical notes and documentation including discharge summaries, lab results and progress notes against SNOMED CT concepts to support the development of clinical AI platforms.

This is a remote, flexible and short-term project.

Key Responsibilities 

- Structured Annotation: Identify clinically relevant concepts across discharge summaries, lab results and prognosis notes, and map them to the correct SNOMED CT codes on a dedicated platform.

- Guideline Application: Work to a coding guideline covering hierarchy scope, negation, medication scope, section-level inclusions and compound coding, applied consistently across a large volume of documents.

- Edge Case Handling: Flag ambiguous or contested cases with a short rationale so guidance can be refined.

- Quality Review: Participate in adjudication rounds to resolve disagreements and reach a consensus code set.

Qualifications: 

License: GMC Registered Doctor based in the UK

title: Corporate Development Director
description:

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation.
